import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Erdős Problem 290

*References:*
- [erdosproblems.com/290](https://www.erdosproblems.com/290)
- [ErGr80] Erdős, P. and Graham, R., *Old and new problems and results in combinatorial number
  theory*. Monographies de L'Enseignement Mathématique (1980), p.34.
- [vD24] van Doorn, W., *On the non-monotonicity of the denominator of generalized harmonic sums*.
  arXiv:2411.03073 (2024).
-/

namespace Erdos290

/-- The denominator (in lowest terms) of the partial harmonic sum
$\sum_{a \leq n \leq b}\frac{1}{n}$. -/
noncomputable def harmonicDen (a b : ℕ) : ℕ := (harmonicBlock a b).den

/--
Let $a\geq 1$. Must there exist some $b>a$ such that
$$\sum_{a\leq n\leq b}\frac{1}{n}=\frac{r_1}{s_1}\textrm{ and }
\sum_{a\leq n\leq b+1}\frac{1}{n}=\frac{r_2}{s_2},$$
with $(r_i,s_i)=1$ and $s_2<s_1$? If so, how does this $b(a)$ grow with $a$?

This was resolved in the affirmative by van Doorn [vD24], who proved $b=b(a)$ always exists, and in
fact $b(a) \ll a$. Indeed, if $a\in (3^k,3^{k+1}]$ then one can take $b=2\cdot 3^{k+1}-1$. van Doorn
also proves that $b(a)>a+(1/2-o(1))\log a$, and considers various generalisations of the original
problem.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at "https://github.com/Woett/Lean-files/blob/main/ErdosProblem290.lean"]
theorem erdos_290 : answer(True) ↔
    (∀ a : ℕ, 1 ≤ a → ∃ b : ℕ, a < b ∧ harmonicDen a (b + 1) < harmonicDen a b) := by
  sorry

end Erdos290

reformulations.difference: The cited van Doorn paper and external proof label a decrease by its later endpoint B, comparing denominators at B and B−1. The reviewed theorem uses the earlier endpoint b and requires a < b.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Set B = b + 1 in one direction and b = B − 1 in the other. The potentially problematic case B = a + 1 cannot be a decrease: for a ≥ 1, harmonicDen a a = a and harmonicDen a (a + 1) = a(a + 1) ≥ a. Thus any later-endpoint witness B > a actually has B − 1 > a. The pointwise equivalence was proved independently of the admitted theorem in /workspace/review/endpoints.lean. The original book already uses the earlier-endpoint convention.

sources_consulted: Erdős and Graham, Old and New Problems and Results in Combinatorial Number Theory (1980), p. 34 (PDF page 30; scan read using OCR): https://mathweb.ucsd.edu/~ronspubs/80_11_number_theory.pdf

W. van Doorn, On the non-monotonicity of the denominator of generalized harmonic sums, arXiv:2411.03073v2, abstract and relevant introduction, definitions, and classical-case results: https://arxiv.org/abs/2411.03073 ; LaTeX source downloaded from https://arxiv.org/e-print/2411.03073
Cited external Lean proof, especially harmonicSum, v, and theorem main: https://raw.githubusercontent.com/Woett/Lean-files/main/ErdosProblem290.lean
review.notes: Both declarations faithfully formalize the existence question. harmonicBlock is the inclusive rational sum, and Rat.den supplies its positive reduced denominator. Zero and empty-interval cases do not affect the theorem. Small computations and kernel-checked examples confirm the boundary case a = 1, b = 5, where the denominator decreases from 60 to 20. After API-only portability edits to a scratch copy of the cited external proof, the exact reviewed proposition kernel-checked using only propext, Classical.choice, and Quot.sound, supporting the solved/True/formal_proof records. The growth question and estimates appear only in explanatory prose. The live erdosproblems.com/290 page remained inaccessible through Cloudflare; the original book and cited paper supplied the mathematical source text. All experiments and proof adaptations were kept under /workspace/review/.
